layers.note: A herb of subalpine meadows and the herb layer of open subalpine forest, spreading in patches from its rhizomes.

heat_load.note: Any aspect; often on cool slopes and at forest edges.

elevation_m.note: Low in the north to subalpine and alpine.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about −20 to 1 °C; gone below −30 °C and above 5 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −42 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −50 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 7 to 18 °C; gone below 5 °C, where summers are too short, and above 21 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 700 to 3,300 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 400.

degree_days_5.note: About 200 to 1,800 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 80.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.45, gone by 0.3.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: summer-dry Cascade summers suit it; up to about 0.6 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.8.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, about 1,650 m) from general knowledge of the species; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Broadleaf arnica grows from Alaska and Yukon to California and Colorado, in moist mountain woods and meadows (the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
